title: Stand up embedded-etcd integration harness for pkg/etcd tests
description: pkg/etcd's only production line any test touches is a nil-receiver Close(); all real ops are untested. Add an integration test harness using go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/embed (or a testcontainers/docker-compose etcd), gated behind a build tag or testing.Short() skip, so subsequent tests run against a REAL etcd per CLAUDE-1 rule 5. Delete the filler TestMockKV and TestContextTimeout (they test a local map and stdlib, not the package).
closure_criteria: A real/embedded etcd starts in the test process; `go test ./pkg/etcd/...` connects and the harness logs a live endpoint with a per-run UUID; TestMockKV/TestContextTimeout are removed from the tree.

title: Prove etcd Put/Get round-trip and missing-key semantics against real etcd
description: Add integration tests: New -> Put(ctx,'k','v') -> Get(ctx,'k') asserts value=='v' && ok==true; then Get of a missing key asserts ok==false, err==nil (covers the len(resp.Kvs)==0 branch at package.go:64).
closure_criteria: Against live etcd, a stored key is read back with exact value and ok==true; a missing-key Get returns ok==false/err==nil; deleting the value-read path makes the test fail.

title: Prove etcd GetPrefix returns exactly matching multi-key set
description: Put a/1, a/2, b/1; assert GetPrefix('a/') returns exactly the two a/ keys with correct values.
closure_criteria: Live etcd GetPrefix('a/') returns the two a/ keys with correct values and excludes b/1; sink-side map asserted.

title: Prove etcd Delete/DeletePrefix remove keys (sink-side absence)
description: Delete then re-Get and assert the key(s) are gone for both Delete and DeletePrefix.
closure_criteria: After Delete/DeletePrefix, a follow-up Get against live etcd shows the key(s) absent (ok==false); test fails if delete is a no-op.

title: Prove etcd Watch fires correct event and closes on ctx cancel
description: Register a watch, Put a new value in another goroutine, assert the received WatchEvent has Type=='PUT', matching Key/Value, Err==nil; also assert the channel closes when ctx is cancelled. The goroutine+channel+ctx-cancel logic at package.go:103-132 is entirely unverified.
closure_criteria: A live Put triggers a WatchEvent with correct Type/Key/Value over the channel; cancelling ctx closes the watch channel; both observed within the test.

title: Prove etcd Lease/PutWithLease/RevokeLease/KeepAlive TTL behavior
description: Put a key with a short lease, assert it is gone after RevokeLease (or TTL expiry); KeepAlive keeps it alive past the TTL window.
closure_criteria: Lease-bound key disappears after RevokeLease/TTL on live etcd; with KeepAlive the key survives past the TTL window; both asserted sink-side.

title: Prove etcd distributed Lock mutual exclusion (highest-risk path)
description: Acquire the lock in goroutine A, assert a second Lock on the same key in goroutine B blocks until A's unlock() is called. The distributed-mutex contract at package.go:172-186 has zero coverage.
closure_criteria: Against live etcd, goroutine B's Lock acquisition timestamp is strictly after A's unlock; B is proven to have blocked while A held the lock.

title: Add mutation-paired etcd New() default-timeout injection test
description: With a real/embedded endpoint, call New(Config{Endpoints:...}) with DialTimeout unset and assert via Raw() config that the 5s default was applied (package.go:26-28), so deleting the default-injection makes the test fail.
closure_criteria: New() with unset DialTimeout yields a client whose effective DialTimeout==5s observed via Raw(); removing the default branch fails the test.

title: Prove etcd error-wrapping on dead endpoint
description: Point New at a dead endpoint with a short DialTimeout and assert operations return the wrapped error (message contains 'etcd ... failed'), proving error wrapping is real.
closure_criteria: Operations against an unreachable endpoint return errors whose message/identity matches the 'etcd ... failed: %w' wrapping; test fails if wrapping is removed.

title: Replace pkg/infra map-echo orchestrator with real service Boot via testcontainers
description: infra Orchestrator performs zero real work — Boot/Health/Logs/Scale/VMSpawn/VMSSH read/write hardcoded strings in a map and tests assert those literals. Use testcontainers-go (or real docker-compose) so Boot('postgres-primary') actually starts Postgres; assert sink-side via a pgx/database/sql connection running SELECT 1, Redis PING, etcd member-list, Kafka produce/consume round-trip.
closure_criteria: Boot('postgres-primary') starts a real Postgres container and a subsequent SELECT 1 over a real connection returns a row; equivalent sink-side probes pass for redis/etcd/kafka; test fails if the service never started.

title: Make pkg/infra Health probe real services and report false on failure
description: Health currently echoes the stored Healthy flag (always true after Boot) and hardcodes Latency=1ms; it can never report unhealthy. Add a test that starts then kills/pauses a service and asserts Health reports Healthy==false with a real measured latency. Add the missing failure-path coverage.
closure_criteria: After a started service is killed/paused, Health() returns Healthy==false with a non-hardcoded measured latency; a healthy service returns true with real probe timing.

title: Make pkg/infra Logs capture real sink-side output honoring tail/since/timestamps
description: Logs returns nil and ignores follow/tail/since/timestamps. Start a service that emits a known marker line, call Logs(..., tail=N), and assert the marker appears and that tail/since/timestamps actually affect the output.
closure_criteria: Logs output contains the known marker line from a real running service, and varying tail/since/timestamps changes the captured output as asserted.

title: Make pkg/infra Scale create real replicas verified via runtime query
description: Scale only writes s.Replicas and a message; no container is created. After Scale(svc,3), query the compose/docker runtime and assert 3 running replicas exist — not just that the struct field equals 3.
closure_criteria: After Scale(svc,3) the docker/compose API reports exactly 3 running replicas for the service; test fails if no real replica is created.

title: Make pkg/infra VMSpawn/VMSSH establish a real session end-to-end
description: VMSpawn fabricates CPU/Memory/IP constants and VMSSH returns a format string with nothing reachable. Spawn a real (or firecracker/QEMU/local-container) node and assert VMSSH runs 'echo ok' over a real session and stdout=='ok'.
closure_criteria: VMSSH executes 'echo ok' over a real SSH session to a spawned node and the captured stdout equals 'ok'; test fails if the host is unreachable.

title: Make pkg/infra VMSimulateFailure/VMSimulatePartition assert observable network effect
description: These flip an in-map string field. Assert an observable network effect instead: a health probe to the node fails during partition and recovers after, rather than only an internal string field.
closure_criteria: During simulated partition a real probe to the node fails; after auto-heal the probe succeeds; both transitions observed, fails if only the string field changed.

title: Add EtcdLocker integration tests against real etcd (block/acquire/lease)
description: pkg/lock's production EtcdLocker (the package's whole reason to exist) has zero coverage. Add tests against REAL etcd: client A holds the lock, client B blocks, A releases, B acquires; assert the etcd key/lease exists while held and is gone after unlock; add error-path test asserting 'etcd lock: %w'/'etcd unlock: %w' wrapping (lock.go:74,78).
closure_criteria: Against live etcd, B acquires only after A releases; the lease key is present while held and absent after unlock (verified via direct etcd Get); error path returns the wrapped message.

title: Rewrite TestMemoryLockerConcurrent to detect a broken lock without -race
description: The concurrent test only asserts counter==10, which survives a no-op lock under the default (non-race) command. Each goroutine, while holding the lock, must set a shared inCritical flag, sleep briefly, and record a violation if another goroutine observed inCritical==true; assert violation count==0. This fails on a no-op lock even without -race.
closure_criteria: Mutating MemoryLocker.Lock to a no-op makes the test FAIL under the default `go test` command (no -race); with the real lock the violation counter is 0.

title: Add explicit block-then-acquire ordering test for MemoryLocker
description: Acquire key, start a goroutine that locks the same key and records a timestamp, sleep, unlock, and assert the second acquisition happened AFTER the unlock — proving the lock serializes rather than just returns.
closure_criteria: The second acquisition timestamp is strictly greater than the unlock timestamp; test fails if Lock returns without blocking.

title: Characterize or fix MemoryLocker.Lock context-cancellation goroutine leak
description: On context cancellation a goroutine is left blocked on lm.Lock() and will later acquire the mutex with no owner to release it (lock.go:44-57). Add a documented test for this leak/behavior, or fix the implementation to not leak and assert the fix.
closure_criteria: Either a test deterministically demonstrates the documented leak behavior, or the implementation is fixed and a test proves no goroutine remains blocked after cancellation.

title: Wire a real Builder behind pkg/build Service and prove image is pullable
description: runBuild is a time.After+magic-string('fail') stub; TestServiceSubmitAndGet asserts State==Succeeded/ImageTag!='' though no image/layer/digest/registry artifact is ever produced. Inject a Builder interface into Service and add an integration test running a real builder (docker buildx/buildkit) against a fixture repo+Dockerfile, asserting the produced image exists and is pullable (sink-side evidence). Alternatively rename the stub path *_Simulated and stop asserting success implies a build.
closure_criteria: A real build of a fixture repo produces an image that can be pulled/inspected from a registry (digest verified); test fails if no real image artifact exists.

title: Drive pkg/build StateFailed via a genuine build failure not the 'fail' sentinel
description: The only path to StateFailed is RepoURL=='fail' (build.go:253). Drive a real failure (invalid Dockerfile / unreachable repo / builder non-zero exit) and assert the error surfaces in Job.Logs and State==StateFailed.
closure_criteria: A real failing build (e.g. bad Dockerfile) yields State==StateFailed with the underlying error captured in Job.Logs; the 'fail' sentinel is no longer the failure trigger.

title: Make pkg/build List/Concurrent tests Start() the service and assert terminal states
description: TestServiceList and TestServiceConcurrentSubmits never call svc.Start(ctx), so workers never run and jobs sit StateQueued; tests only count map size and swallow Submit errors. Start the service, wait for terminal states, assert each job reached StateSucceeded, check Submit return values, and add a queue-overflow test asserting 'build queue is full'.
closure_criteria: With Start(ctx), all submitted jobs reach StateSucceeded; Submit errors are asserted not discarded; filling the 100-slot queue returns 'build queue is full'.

title: Replace time.Sleep polling in pkg/build with completion sync and add state-machine mutation tests
description: Tests depend on a 100ms simulated build finishing inside a 300ms sleep (flaky-by-construction). Replace time.Sleep with a completion channel/Job.Done(); add a mutation test that fails if TransitionTo validation or IsTerminal is removed (queued->succeeded rejected, terminal re-transition rejected, StartedAt/CompletedAt set by the worker).
closure_criteria: Tests synchronize on real completion (no fixed sleeps); removing TransitionTo validation or IsTerminal makes a test fail; timestamps set by the worker are asserted.

title: Enforce or document pkg/build content-addressable cache digest integrity
description: DiskCache.Put/MemoryCache.Put accept any digest string for any data; content-addressability claimed in the package doc is unenforced. Add a test asserting Get rejects (or is documented not to verify) Digest(data)==digest; if it is a real guarantee, enforce it in Put/Get and test the mismatch rejection.
closure_criteria: Storing data under a mismatched digest is rejected on Get (or behavior is explicitly documented and tested); test fails if a corrupted/mismatched digest is silently accepted as a guarantee.

title: Cover pkg/build cancel-mid-flight branch sets StateCancelled
description: Add a test that cancels a job while runBuild is in-flight and asserts the context-cancellation branch (build.go:246-249) sets StateCancelled and logs 'cancelled' — currently uncovered.
closure_criteria: Cancelling an in-flight job transitions it to StateCancelled with a 'cancelled' log entry; test fails if the cancel branch is removed.

title: Add real mTLS handshake test for pkg/security (valid client succeeds, no/foreign cert rejected)
description: mTLS is never handshaked — tests only inspect *tls.Config fields. Using generateTestCert, start a TLS server with ServerTLS() and assert: a client from ClientTLS() (valid same-CA cert) completes the handshake and exchanges a byte; a client with no cert or a foreign-CA cert is REJECTED with a handshake error. This is the sink-side proof that RequireAndVerifyClientCert enforces mutual auth.
closure_criteria: A same-CA client exchanges a byte over a real tls.Listener/tls.Dial; a no-cert/foreign-CA client fails the handshake with an error; both observed in one test.

title: Assert MinVersion==TLS13 on the client TLS path in pkg/security
description: TestClientTLS checks len(Certificates)==1 and RootCAs!=nil but does NOT assert MinVersion==tls.VersionTLS13 (unlike the server test). Add the assertion so the client TLS-1.3 floor has a mutation pair.
closure_criteria: ClientTLS() config asserts MinVersion==tls.VersionTLS13; removing the TLS 1.3 floor on the client path fails the test.

title: Locate/build production Vault client and add dev-Vault integration test (KVv2 + PKI)
description: vault.go ships only an interface+wrapper+mock; no production VaultClient exists in-package, and all Vault tests drive MockVaultClient with hand-fed values. Confirm/locate the production client and add an integration test against a real Vault (dev-mode container) exercising KVv2 read/write round-trip and PKI issue->renew, asserting the returned Certificate PEM parses via x509.ParseCertificate. If none exists, mark the Vault feature incomplete rather than imply complete via green mock tests.
closure_criteria: Against a dev Vault, a KVv2 secret is written and read back identically, and a PKI-issued cert PEM parses successfully via x509.ParseCertificate; or the feature is explicitly marked incomplete.

title: Replace pkg/security non-nil-only TestNewTLSConfigBuilder with meaningful assertion
description: TestNewTLSConfigBuilder only asserts the constructor returns non-nil (it cannot return nil), proving nothing. Replace with an assertion that the stored PEM bytes are actually used (covered transitively by the handshake test).
closure_criteria: The builder test asserts a behavioral property (PEM bytes used in the produced config) rather than non-nil; removing the test loses no coverage already provided by the handshake test.

title: Verify pkg/hxcregistry item_history audit-sink rows after Create/Update
description: CreateItem/UpdateItem write item_history rows with swallowed errors (_, _ = r.db.Exec) and no test ever queries them, so the audit-history feature could be entirely broken while tests pass. Query item_history after CreateItem asserting exactly one row with event_type='Opened'; after UpdateItem assert an 'Updated' row; stop swallowing those Exec errors.
closure_criteria: After Create, a SELECT on item_history returns one row with event_type='Opened'; after Update, an 'Updated' row exists; Exec errors are surfaced not swallowed; test fails if history writes are broken.

title: Assert exact and stable ComputeHeadingHash value in pkg/hxcregistry
description: Hash is asserted only !='' so any non-empty garbage passes and the 'stable hash for re-sync binding' claim is unproven. Assert ComputeHeadingHash of a known title equals a known 16-hex constant, equals itself on repeated calls, and that two different titles produce different hashes (mutation-paired).
closure_criteria: ComputeHeadingHash('<known title>') equals a pinned 16-hex value, is identical across calls, and differs for a different title; test fails on any digest change.

title: Add pkg/hxcregistry failure-path tests (dup PK, missing-id Get/Update)
description: Happy-path only today. Add: second CreateItem with duplicate HXCID returns an error; GetItem('HXC-999') returns the 'not found' error (hits sql.ErrNoRows branch registry.go:155-157); UpdateItem on a non-existent id either errors or is asserted as a documented no-op via RowsAffected.
closure_criteria: Duplicate-PK insert errors; missing-id Get returns the not-found error; missing-id Update behavior is asserted (error or documented no-op via RowsAffected).

title: Make pkg/hxcregistry concurrent test do concurrent writes (or rename)
description: TestRegistryConcurrentAccess only spawns concurrent reads against one row despite its name. Run concurrent CreateItem/UpdateItem with distinct ids and assert all rows present and consistent (final count==N), or rename it to TestRegistryConcurrentReads.
closure_criteria: Concurrent writes of N distinct items leave exactly N consistent rows under -race; or the test is renamed to reflect read-only scope.

title: Prove pkg/hxcregistry timestamp round-trip and DB CHECK-constraint enforcement
description: Assert LastModified strictly increased after UpdateItem and CreatedAt round-trips through RFC3339 store/load. Add a DB-constraint test inserting an invalid current_location/status directly to prove the schema CHECK constraints are active (sink-side enforcement vs Go-side Validate divergence).
closure_criteria: LastModified advances after Update and CreatedAt survives round-trip; a direct insert violating current_location/status CHECK is rejected by the DB.

title: Wire pkg/wasm WasmPlugin.Execute to real WASM output and prove transformed result
description: Execute calls host.Call but discards the WASM return and returns input unchanged; TestWasmPluginLifecycle asserts the literal it passed in. Make Execute use the real WASM return value/linear memory, then test a module whose execute transforms input (e.g. len*2 or a memory write) and assert the TRANSFORMED result so an ignored WASM call FAILS the test.
closure_criteria: A WASM module that transforms its input produces a transformed output through Execute that differs from the input; the test fails if Execute ignores the WASM call.

title: Add pkg/wasm negative tests for missing execute export and corrupt module Init
description: Add a negative test where the module lacks the execute export and confirm Execute surfaces ErrFunctionNotFound (currently init/shutdown/execute absence is silently tolerated). Add an Init failure test loading a structurally invalid .wasm and asserting Init returns a wrapped error (proving the load/instantiate error path, not just the host==nil guard).
closure_criteria: Missing-execute-export module makes Execute return ErrFunctionNotFound; corrupt .wasm bytes make Init return a wrapped error.

title: Prove pkg/wasm init/shutdown exports actually run via memory side-effect
description: Init and Shutdown swallow the result/error of init/shutdown exports; no test verifies they were invoked. Use a WASM module that records a side effect (writes a sentinel to exported memory) and verify after Init/Shutdown the sentinel changed, so removing the h.Call(initFn)/h.Call(shutdown) lines fails a test.
closure_criteria: An exported-memory sentinel changes after Init and again after Shutdown; removing either h.Call line fails the test.

title: Cover pkg/wasm Host.Call ErrUnexpectedResult branch
description: Add a test covering Host.Call's ErrUnexpectedResult branch (a function returning a non-i64/multi-value result), currently uncovered.
closure_criteria: A module function returning a non-i64/multi-value result causes Host.Call to return ErrUnexpectedResult; test fails if the branch is removed.

title: Replace self-defeating pkg/semaphore TestSemaphore_ReleaseTooMany_Mutation
description: The over-release test accepts both immediate-return and timeout branches and asserts nothing, so it can never fail and it leaks a permanently-blocked goroutine. Replace with a test that asserts the honest contract — Release() on an unheld semaphore blocks (fail if the done channel closes early) — and cleans up the goroutine, or change the API to make over-release detectable and test the detection.
closure_criteria: The new test fails if Release() on an unheld semaphore returns early; the previously leaked goroutine is cleaned up; the test has a real assertion that can fail.

title: Add pkg/semaphore M>>N concurrency invariant test under -race
description: No concurrency/race coverage exists despite the type's purpose. Launch M>>N goroutines that each Acquire(), increment a counter, assert the active count never exceeds N (atomic load + peak tracker), then Release(); run the package under -race.
closure_criteria: Under `go test -race`, the observed peak concurrent holders never exceeds N across M>>N goroutines; a counting bug would be caught.

title: Add pkg/semaphore New(0) barrier and exact-capacity boundary tests
description: Add New(0) cases (TryAcquire returns false, Acquire blocks indefinitely) and verify TryAcquire count exactly equals N before returning false; add a round-trip test that after K matched Acquire/Release pairs the semaphore returns to empty (TryAcquire succeeds exactly N times).
closure_criteria: New(0) TryAcquire returns false and Acquire blocks; TryAcquire succeeds exactly N times on a fresh New(N); state returns to baseline after matched pairs.

title: Convert pkg/storage error tests to errors.Is on exported sentinels
description: Five error tests only assert err!=nil; the exported sentinels ErrKeyNotFound/ErrEmptyKey are never proven, so a wrong wrapped/generic error would still pass. Switch each to errors.Is(err, ErrKeyNotFound)/errors.Is(err, ErrEmptyKey) to lock the public error contract.
closure_criteria: Each error test asserts the specific sentinel via errors.Is; returning a different error type fails the test.

title: Reconcile and test pkg/storage FileStore vs MemoryStore copy semantics
description: MemoryStore copies data in/out (paired tests) but FileStore.Put writes the caller slice directly and Get returns the freshly-read slice; the divergent aliasing semantics are unproven. Add TestFileStorePutCopiesData/GetCopiesData OR document+assert that FileStore intentionally does not copy, making the two implementations' contract explicit and tested.
closure_criteria: FileStore copy behavior is asserted (either copies, with mutation-paired tests, or documented non-copy with a test pinning it); a Store conformance contract is explicit.

title: Add pkg/storage overwrite, missing-delete, and List edge tests for both stores
description: Add overwrite tests (Put(k,v1);Put(k,v2);Get(k)==v2) for both stores; TestDeleteMissingKeyIsNoError for the intentional idempotent-delete contract; List('') returns-all and List('nomatch') returns-empty-no-error; remove or test the ineffective FileStore.List dir-Stat branch (storage.go:151-154).
closure_criteria: Overwrite returns v2 for both stores; deleting a missing key returns nil; List('') returns all keys and List('nomatch') returns empty/no error; the dead dir-Stat branch is removed or covered.

title: Add pkg/storage -race concurrent Put/Get/Delete test to prove RWMutex
description: Both stores carry sync.RWMutex implying thread-safety, but the locking could be removed and every test would still pass. Add a -race concurrent Put/Get/Delete test (N goroutines); optionally a table-driven Store conformance suite run against both NewMemoryStore() and NewFileStore(t.TempDir()).
closure_criteria: Under `go test -race`, concurrent Put/Get/Delete across N goroutines is clean; removing the RWMutex triggers a race detector failure.

title: Gate -race in CI for pkg/metrics concurrency mutation tests
description: TestCounter/Gauge/Histogram_Concurrent*_Mutation only assert final aggregates and pass even with atomics removed because the audit run lacks -race. Add a `go test -race ./pkg/metrics/...` CI job and document that these tests are only meaningful under -race.
closure_criteria: A CI job runs pkg/metrics under -race; removing an atomic/lock triggers a race detector failure in that job.

title: Complete pkg/metrics Prometheus exposition assertions (+Inf, _sum, ordering)
description: TestPrometheusHandler checks one finite bucket line and _count but never asserts the _bucket{le='+Inf'} line, the _sum line, or the %g float formatting; a regression dropping +Inf or _sum would still pass. Assert the +Inf bucket, _sum, exact _count, and the full ordered body (golden string) so dropped lines fail.
closure_criteria: The handler test asserts +Inf bucket, _sum, _count, and a deterministic ordered body; dropping any required line fails the test.

title: Add pkg/metrics duplicate-registration and histogram edge tests
description: Add TestRegistry_DuplicateName pinning intended overwrite-or-reject semantics, TestRegistry_Serialize_Ordering for sorted multi-type output, and histogram edge tests: empty buckets, unsorted buckets, Observe(Inf)/Observe(NaN), and a boundary-equality case (v==bucket) proving <= cumulative semantics.
closure_criteria: Duplicate-name semantics asserted; ordered multi-type body asserted; histogram edge/boundary cases produce the documented behavior with tests that fail on regression.

title: Add pkg/metrics /metrics integration test via httptest.Server
description: Mount PrometheusHandler() on a real httptest.Server, issue an HTTP GET, and validate the parsed body — proving end-user /metrics scrape behavior, not just in-process handler invocation.
closure_criteria: An HTTP GET to a real server hosting PrometheusHandler() returns a parseable Prometheus body with the expected metrics.

title: Test pkg/grpcutil LoggingStreamInterceptor recv/send counters
description: LoggingStreamInterceptor + wrappedStream (the only function producing real sink-side state) are entirely untested; recvCount/sendCount could be a no-op and all tests pass. Drive RecvMsg/SendMsg N and M times and assert the emitted log line contains recv=N send=M (capture via log.SetOutput) AND assert ws.recvCount/ws.sendCount directly.
closure_criteria: After N RecvMsg and M SendMsg calls, the log line contains recv=N send=M and the counter fields equal N/M; a no-op counter fails the test.

title: Strengthen pkg/grpcutil log assertions to dynamic behavior-dependent fields
description: TestUnaryInterceptorCallsHandler/Stream only assert Contains('unary')/('stream') which are hardcoded literals always present regardless of branch. Assert dynamic fields: Contains('/test/Method'), Contains('code=OK'), Contains('err=<nil>') so the assertion fails if the wrong branch runs.
closure_criteria: Log assertions check method path, code=OK, and err=<nil>; an incorrect branch (missing auth/duration/code) fails the test.

title: Cover pkg/grpcutil status.FromError code extraction for handler errors
description: The code-extraction logging path (package.go:33-37, 58-62) is never verified because rejection tests short-circuit on auth. Add a test where the handler returns status.Error(codes.Internal, ...) and assert the interceptor returns that exact code and logs code=Internal for both unary and stream. Also add TestAuthUnaryInterceptorEmptyTokenSlice for the len(tokens)==0 branch.
closure_criteria: Handler returning codes.Internal is propagated with code=Internal logged for unary and stream; empty-token-slice metadata is rejected via the len==0 branch.

title: Add pkg/context TestDetach_PreservesValues for the value-retention guarantee
description: The headline guarantee — Detach 'keeps only values' — is never tested; a mutation returning context.Background() would pass everything. Store a value in the parent, cancel the parent, and assert the value survives through the detached context.
closure_criteria: parent:=WithValue(...); d:=Detach(parent); cancel parent; d.Value(key)=='v' still holds; a Detach returning Background() fails the test.

title: Strengthen pkg/context WithTimeout deadline and expiry assertions
description: TestWithTimeout only checks Deadline() ok==true, near-tautological. Assert the deadline is within tolerance of now+timeout, add a positive-duration expiry test (wait for Done() to fire, assert Err()==DeadlineExceeded), and a cancel-path test asserting Err()==context.Canceled after cancel().
closure_criteria: Deadline ~= now+timeout within tolerance; a real short timeout fires Done() with DeadlineExceeded; cancel() yields Canceled; a hardcoded/ignored timeout fails the test.

title: Give pkg/workerpool TestPool_NilWorkSafe_Mutation a real sink
description: The nil-work test has no assertion and relies on non-deterministic no-panic. Follow the nil submission with a non-nil submission that signals a channel and assert the worker survived and processed the subsequent task, so removing the if fn!=nil guard is reliably caught.
closure_criteria: After a nil submission, a follow-up task signals completion proving the worker survived; removing the nil guard fails the test deterministically.

title: Add pkg/workerpool fan-in count==N, post-Stop Submit, panic-recovery, idempotent-Stop tests
description: Submit blocks forever after Stop (goroutine leak), a panicking task crashes the process (no recover in worker()), and double-Stop panics on close(stopCh). Add: fan-in test asserting final counter==N after Stop (no task dropped); post-Stop Submit hang guard (Submit in a goroutine with timeout); panicking-task recovery (add recover() in worker() then assert pool keeps processing); idempotent double-Stop (guard the close) with a test calling Stop() twice.
closure_criteria: N submitted tasks all execute (counter==N); a post-Stop Submit is shown not to hang; a panicking task is recovered and later tasks still run; Stop() called twice does not panic.

title: Make pkg/errors concurrency test honest via locked GetFields path + -race
description: TestConcurrentFieldAccess reads err.Fields directly without RLock, runs without -race, and asserts nothing, so it proves nothing about the mutex. Route concurrent readers through GetFields (locked path), assert len(GetFields(err))==50 (all writes observed), and CI-gate -race for the package.
closure_criteria: Readers use GetFields; after the run len(GetFields(err))==50; under -race the mutex is exercised and removing it triggers a race failure.

title: Pin pkg/errors Code enum exact values, distinctness, and WithFields nil receiver
description: TestCodeEnumValues only checks non-empty (collisions/renames pass). Assert exact string values (e.g. E_NOT_FOUND=='E_NOT_FOUND') and pairwise distinctness via a set. Add TestWithFields_NilReceiver covering the e==nil guard (package.go:139), an errors.As chain extraction test, GetFields(nil) returns empty non-nil map, and a stack-frame-content + 32-frame-cap assertion.
closure_criteria: Each Code equals its exact expected string and all are distinct; WithFields nil receiver is safe; errors.As extracts *Error through a Wrap chain; GetFields(nil) returns empty non-nil; stack content/cap asserted.

title: Replace tautological pkg/backoff cap-mutation test and pin Default()
description: TestDuration_CapRemoved_Mutation uses Max=1<<62 so output is byte-identical whether the cap branch exists or not. Replace with a small-Max test (Base=100ms,Max=500ms,Factor=2) asserting Duration(20)==500ms exactly. Pin Default() to exact Base=100ms/Max=30s/Factor=2 and Default().Duration(1)==200ms; add monotonic-growth and an exact mid-range (Duration(3)==800ms) assertion.
closure_criteria: Removing the cap branch makes Duration(20)!=500ms and the test fails; Default() exact fields asserted; monotonic growth and Duration(3)==800ms hold.

title: Assert pkg/classads parser AST Op per operator and paren precedence
description: Parser tests assert only err==nil, never the resulting Op/tree shape (a <-parsed-as-> mutation survives), and no eval-level paren test proves precedence override. Assert expr.(BinaryOp).Op per comparison operator; add Eval('(1+2)*3',nil)==9 paired with Eval('1+2*3',nil)==7; assert TestParseLogical root is BinaryOp{Op:'||'} with both children &&.
closure_criteria: Each comparison operator parses to the correct Op; (1+2)*3 evaluates to 9 and 1+2*3 to 7; logical tree shape asserted; a <->> swap fails a test.

title: Add pkg/classads eval failure-path and regexp non-match tests
description: Add failure-path eval tests for guarded type mismatches: Eval('!5') errors ('! requires bool'), Eval('"x" < 1') errors ('requires numbers'), regexp with a non-string arg errors. Add a Match test where the requirement evaluates to a non-bool asserting the 'did not evaluate to bool' error (eval.go:26). Add a regexp non-match case (regexp('^win','linux')==false).
closure_criteria: Each guarded mismatch returns the documented error; non-bool Match returns the bool-error; regexp non-match returns false; removing a validation branch fails a test.

title: Add pkg/crypto SHA-256 known-answer vectors and sentinel errors.Is checks
description: Hash/GenerateKey assert length only (a deterministic-but-wrong digest passes) and sentinel errors are never checked via errors.Is. Add SHA-256 KAT (Hash('abc')==ba7816bf...); assert ErrVerifyFailed/ErrInvalidKey/ErrInvalidCiphertext via errors.Is; replace negative-path err discards with t.Fatalf.
closure_criteria: Hash('abc') equals the published SHA-256 vector; negative paths assert the specific sentinel via errors.Is; a wrong-but-deterministic digest fails the test.

title: Add pkg/crypto AES-128/192, wrong-key decrypt, short-ciphertext, PBKDF2 vector tests
description: Only AES-256 is covered. Add table-driven AES-128 (16-byte) and AES-192 (24-byte) keys plus an invalid-key-length rejection case; a wrong-key decrypt (encrypt with A, decrypt with B -> auth failure) proving key binding; a 'ciphertext too short' test (hex shorter than gcm.NonceSize()) hitting the ErrInvalidCiphertext length branch; a fixed PBKDF2 vector for DeriveKey.
closure_criteria: AES-128/192 round-trip; wrong-key decrypt fails with auth error; short ciphertext yields ErrInvalidCiphertext; DeriveKey matches a fixed PBKDF2 vector.

title: Add pkg/log prefix-field proof catching the SetLevel prefix-loss bug
description: Real bug: SetLevel rebuilds the handler with hardcoded .With('logger','helix'), dropping the New(prefix) value; no test asserts the logger field survives SetLevel. Add a test that New('svc',&buf) emits JSON containing 'logger':'svc', and a mutation-paired test where after SetLevel(WarnLevel) the emitted record still has logger=='svc' (this fails today at package.go:100).
closure_criteria: Emitted JSON contains 'logger':'svc' from New('svc',...) and still does after SetLevel; the current SetLevel prefix-loss bug is caught (test fails until fixed).

title: Strengthen pkg/log Warn test, add Debug-suppression, remove dead captureOutput scaffolding
description: TestWarn only checks a message substring. Strengthen it to assert a structured field reaches output and add a TestWarn_Mutation for field-dropping; add a Debug-suppression test (SetLevel(InfoLevel) then Debug produces empty output). Remove or wire up the dead captureOutput/defaultOutput scaffolding (package_test.go:11-20). Optionally test Fatal via subprocess.
closure_criteria: Warn emits and asserts a structured field; Debug is suppressed at InfoLevel; dead scaffolding is removed; field-drop mutation fails the Warn test.

title: Add pkg/lru boundary, cold-miss, and struct-value round-trip tests
description: lru has no pass-bluffs but minor gaps. Add NewCache(0)/NewCache(-1) boundary tests asserting intended degenerate behavior (pins the eviction guard at package.go:43); an explicit cold-miss test (fresh cache Get('absent') returns nil,false at package.go:33); a struct-value round-trip proving the interface{} value path; optionally a -race test if used concurrently or document non-thread-safety.
closure_criteria: NewCache(0)/(-1) behavior asserted; fresh-cache miss returns (nil,false); a struct value round-trips by equality; concurrency stance is tested or documented.

title: Add pkg/pubsub -race concurrency test and explicit drop-boundary assertion
description: No -race concurrency test exists despite the RWMutex being the main correctness mechanism, and the 10-retained/11th-dropped boundary is not explicit. Add a -race test: N subscribers / M publishers over overlapping subjects with deterministic per-subscriber counts; add a boundary test draining the channel to assert exactly the first 10 messages retained and the 11th dropped; add an unknown-subject no-op test.
closure_criteria: Under -race, concurrent subscribe/publish is clean and per-subscriber counts are deterministic; draining shows exactly 10 retained and 11th dropped; publish to an unsubscribed subject is a safe no-op.

title: Prove pkg/ratelimit bucket starts full and add Limiter conformance + -race tests
description: TestTokenBucket_ZeroTokensInitially_Mutation only asserts one Allow succeeds (would pass if bucket started with 1 token). Assert NewTokenBucket(5,0) allows exactly 5 then denies the 6th. Add var _ Limiter=(*PerKeyLimiter)(nil) conformance and reconcile TokenBucket/SlidingWindow with the Limiter interface; add a -race test that total granted tokens never exceeds max under concurrent AllowN; add a denied-AllowN no-side-effect test for SlidingWindow.
closure_criteria: NewTokenBucket(5,0) grants exactly 5 then denies; a value used through the Limiter interface compiles/runs; under -race total granted never exceeds max; a denied AllowN leaves window slots unconsumed.

title: Bring pkg/retry DoWithResult to behavioral parity with Do
description: DoWithResult is a duplicated loop with near-zero coverage: TestDoWithResultExhausted only asserts err!=nil; its non-retryable branch (retry.go:98) and context-cancellation branch (retry.go:104-108) are unexercised. Add DoWithResult mutation mirrors of the Do tests: exact attempt count, errors.Is last-error wrapping, zero-value-on-failure, context-cancellation early-abort (callCount check), and an exponential-timing test.
closure_criteria: DoWithResult tests assert exact attempt count, errors.Is wrapping, zero-value on failure, early-abort on cancel, and backoff timing; a regression in its loop fails a test.

title: Add pkg/retry transient-recovery, jitter-bound, and computeDelay table tests
description: Add transient-recovery tests for both Do and DoWithResult (fail K then succeed, assert success/value and callCount==K+1). Strengthen TestDoExhausted-class with errors.Is(sentinel) and attempt-count. Add a jitter upper-bound test (every per-attempt delay in [D,1.25D)) and a tiny-delay (Delay=1ns) edge to pin the rand.Int63n(.../4) panic. Add a computeDelay table (Fixed/Linear/Exponential/default+MaxDelay clamp) asserting exact durations with jitter disabled.
closure_criteria: Transient recovery proven for both variants; exhaustion tests assert sentinel+count; jitter never exceeds 1.25D and tiny-delay does not panic; computeDelay table matches exact durations.

title: Strengthen pkg/serde MustMarshal exact-content and add Unmarshal failure tests
description: TestMustMarshal asserts only len!=0 (garbage would pass). Replace with an exact-content assertion (string(data)=='{"k":"v"}'). Add an Unmarshal failure-path test feeding malformed JSON asserting a non-nil error; add a nested/tagged round-trip (slices, maps, nested structs, json:'-'/omitempty); optionally assert Unmarshal into nil/non-pointer returns an error.
closure_criteria: MustMarshal output equals the exact expected JSON; malformed input to Unmarshal returns a non-nil error; nested/tagged round-trip preserves structure; nil/non-pointer target errors.

title: Pin pkg/validator error contract via errors.Is and remove/wire unused sentinels
description: Tests assert only err!=nil/substring, so the wrong sentinel or dropped %w would pass; ErrMinExceeded/ErrMaxExceeded are declared but never returned (checkMin/checkMax use ad-hoc fmt.Errorf) — a latent API lie. Convert assertions to errors.Is on each sentinel; either wire ErrMinExceeded/ErrMaxExceeded through %w with a matching errors.Is test or delete them.
closure_criteria: Each validation failure asserts its specific sentinel via errors.Is; ErrMinExceeded/ErrMaxExceeded are either returned (with a passing errors.Is test) or removed; a wrong-sentinel return fails a test.

title: Add pkg/validator uint min/max, IsValidID empty, oneof/email boundary tests
description: Add uint min/max cases (uint8/uint64) to cover the dedicated reflect.Uint* branches (validator.go:185-189,211-215); IsValidID('') expecting false plus an underscore/dash positive case; an email boundary ('a@b' accepted by net/mail, 'user@' rejected); a registered-custom-rule-with-required ordering test and a test that an unregistered rule name is silently ignored (checkRule default fall-through, line 168), documenting/pinning that behavior.
closure_criteria: uint min/max branches covered; IsValidID('') is false; email boundaries behave per net/mail; unregistered rule names are pinned as silently ignored; removing a reflect.Uint branch fails a test.

title: Establish fleet-wide -race CI gate across concurrency-sensitive packages
description: Systemic gap: concurrency/atomicity guarantees are 'proven' by count-only tests that pass even with the lock/atomic removed because the audit command does not run -race (affects errors, metrics, semaphore, storage, lock, pubsub, ratelimit). Add a CI job running `go test -race ./...` (or per-package -race jobs) so a removed lock/atomic is detected fleet-wide, not per-package.
closure_criteria: A CI pipeline runs the suite under -race; introducing a deliberate data race (remove a mutex/atomic in any listed package) causes the -race job to fail with a detected race, evidenced by the CI log and a per-run UUID.
